A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniDrive-WM, with matching core methods and identifiable corresponding experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original Bench2Drive planning, perception, image-generation, and VQA results, including closed-loop evaluations and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains original Bench2Drive experiments and reports additional nuScenes results, DriveLM GVQA evaluations, and a planning/generation-order ablation.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the QT-Former/VLM backbone, Gaussian latent trajectory planner without KL regularization, planning-conditioned generation, AR and AR+Diffusion alternatives, and the same joint objectives. v4's expanded perception and planner appendices disclose implementation details without establishing a changed default algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates on Bench2Drive and its Chat-B2D annotations; mentioning nuScenes detection metrics does not establish nuScenes evaluation. v4 adds actual nuScenes training/evaluation for planning and future-image generation, plus DriveLM GVQA evaluation. This substantially extends coverage from simulated driving to real-world data and another understanding benchmark.

E2.justification: v4 adds a nuScenes planning comparison involving Drive-VLM, Doe-1, OmniDrive, and FSDrive alongside retained planning baselines. Its new GVQA comparison includes the DriveLM baseline, Cube-LLM, TrackingMeetsLMM, SimpleLLM4AD, OmniDrive, and FSDrive. The corresponding Bench2Drive baseline sets and image-generation comparator set remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated AR+Diffusion output resolution from 256×256 to 512×1024, materially changing its experimental setting. v4 also introduces the official nuScenes train/validation split, DriveLM GVQA metrics, an ordering-control experiment, and A100 inference-speed measurements. The Bench2Drive 950/50 split and 220-route protocol remain unchanged; collision values converted to percentages do not constitute a new metric.

E4.justification: v4 Table 7 adds a focused ablation testing whether planning should precede image generation, comparing both orders on trajectory error, collisions, and FID. Section 4.5 also quantifies the architectures' speed trade-off. The earlier module-removal and Chat-B2D image-generation ablations are retained, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Gaussian latent variables and v2's qualitative discussion of diffusion variance are not statistical uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: v4 adds nuScenes and GVQA results and revises existing scores. Bench2Drive FID changes from 6.4 to 7.2 for AR and from 7.1 to 6.6 for AR+Diffusion (v2 Table 3; v4 Table 4). AR+Diffusion's 3-second L2 changes from 1.092 to 1.066, with its stated resolution also changing. Chat-B2D CIDEr/BLEU/ROUGE-L change from 66.3/52.9/78.3 to 66.7/53.5/78.6. v4 newly reports nuScenes average L2 of 0.30/0.29 for the two branches and a GVQA final score of 0.59. Percentage conversions in retained collision results are equivalent representations.

T1.justification: Equation (4) changes the memory bank's first time index from t−n to t−n+1, correcting its consistency with the stated n-frame bank. The principal probabilistic formulations and losses remain equivalent, and neither version introduces theoretical guarantees or proofs. The expanded cosine-similarity expression is mathematically unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions—unified understanding, planning, and generation with two decoding alternatives—remain intact. The abstract strengthens its claimed L2/collision reductions from 5.9%/9.2% to 7.3%/10.4%, while the introduction extends its stated planning-performance claim to nuScenes as well as Bench2Drive.

C2.justification: v2 attributes AR's better planning results to more explicit token-space supervision. v4 instead explains AR+Diffusion's revised advantage through continuous geometric detail and reduced exposure bias, while positioning AR for reactive control and AR+Diffusion for slower, high-fidelity or offline use. It additionally interprets the ordering ablation through the action-to-observation causal direction and the new real-world results as evidence of generalization.

D1.justification: v4 Appendices C–D substantially expand implementation disclosure: Hungarian matching and focal/L1 perception-pretraining losses, Gaussian MLP parameterization and reparameterization, a recurrent BEV waypoint decoder, and how planning losses use detected boxes and lane boundaries. These clarify previously underspecified components rather than establish new ones. v4 also supplies A100 inference speeds of 2 fps for AR and 0.4 fps for AR+Diffusion; the project-page access information is equivalent.

R1.justification: v4 updates the literature discussion with works such as DriveVLA-W0, DriveVA, VLGA, G2DP, OccSim, and navigation world models, and adds references supporting the new benchmarks and baselines. The three related-work categories and the central positioning around jointly modeling trajectories and visual futures remain unchanged, making this a contextual expansion rather than a fundamental repositioning.

P1.justification: v4 substantially reorganizes the experimental narrative: planning, generation, and VQA results are consolidated; the scattered AR/diffusion discussion becomes a dedicated comparison section; metric definitions move to Appendix A; and the Chat-B2D ablation moves into the main text. The perception appendix is rewritten and subdivided, and planner explanations are expanded. Much of the introduction, core method, and conclusion remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting, with extensively rescaled and relocated displays. Figure 1 is recomposed, generation figures incorporate or replace examples with nuScenes imagery, and new qualitative Figures 7–8 appear. New benchmark and ordering-ablation tables are added, while the old standalone architecture-comparison table is redistributed across other comparisons. Some tables and the retained VQA figure become visibly smaller.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses an important weakness of v2's predominantly simulation-based validation by adding real-world nuScenes planning/generation results and DriveLM GVQA comparisons. The ordering ablation directly tests a central design choice, and Appendices C–D materially improve implementation transparency. These gains substantially strengthen the paper's evidence and inspectability. Changed decoder resolution and continued absence of run statistics limit architectural comparisons, and some displays lose legibility, but these limitations do not outweigh the broader validation and clearer documentation.
